request.title: Add a rename command
request.body: Add a command, rename, that changes the title of a task: rename followed by the task id and the new title, for example: rename 2 Call Sam back. It replies "Renamed 2: Call Sam back". The new title is trimmed the same way as in add, and an empty new title is an error that leaves the task as it was. An id that does not exist is an error with the same message the other commands give ("No task with id 7"), and something that is not an id is an error with the message they give ("Not a task id: abc"). Renaming changes only the title: the task keeps its id, whether it is done, and its place in the list. Everything that works today must keep working. Plain ES modules, no dependencies.

artifact.title: Add a rename command to the task CLI
artifact.problem: The task CLI can create tasks but cannot change a task's title once it exists. A typo or a change of wording is stuck, and recreating the task would lose its id, its done state, and its place in the list. Users need a way to correct or update a task's title in place.
goals: Add a rename command that takes a task id and a new title and changes that task's title.
Confirm a successful rename with a reply in the form "Renamed <id>: <new title>".
Reuse existing input conventions: title trimming as in add, and the existing error messages for unknown ids and non-id arguments.
Touch only the title: the task's id, done state, and position in the list are preserved.
Keep every behavior that works today working unchanged.
nonGoals: Renaming more than one task at a time (no ranges, wildcards, or bulk operations).
Interactive title editing such as an editor or prompt; the new title comes only from the command arguments.
Changing anything other than the title: ids, done state, ordering, and the task's place in the list are not affected by rename.
Undo, history, or audit trail for renames.
Changes to other commands, their output, or their behavior.
constraints: Plain ES modules; no new dependencies and no build step.
The rename command's error messages must match the existing commands' messages exactly: "No task with id <id>" for an unknown id and "Not a task id: <argument>" for an argument that is not an id.
Trimming of the new title must behave exactly like the add command's trimming of a task title.
The request does not prescribe the exact error message for an empty new title; the command must report an error in the CLI's existing error style and leave the task unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Given a task with id 2 exists, running "rename 2 Call Sam back" replies "Renamed 2: Call Sam back", and the task with id 2 has the title "Call Sam back" when the task list is read afterwards; the reply for a successful rename always has the form "Renamed <id>: <new title>".

After a successful rename, the renamed task keeps its id, keeps its done or not-done state (a done task stays done), and keeps its position in the list relative to the other tasks; no other task is changed.
The new title is the whole text after the task id and may contain spaces: for a task with id 3, "rename 3 Buy milk, eggs, and bread" gives it the title "Buy milk, eggs, and bread".

The new title is trimmed the same way add trims a new task's title: for example "rename 2   Call Sam back   " gives task 2 the title "Call Sam back", and the trimming behaves identically to what add produces for a task title with the same padding.

When the new title is missing or empty after trimming, for example "rename 2" or "rename 2   ", the command reports an error and the task is left exactly as it was, including its title, id, done state, and position.
When the id given to rename matches no task, for example "rename 7 Call Sam back" with no task 7, the command replies "No task with id 7" and no task changes.
When the first argument after rename is not a task id, for example "rename abc Call Sam back", the command replies "Not a task id: abc" and no task changes.
When rename is invoked with no arguments, the command reports an error and no task changes.
Every command available before this change continues to accept the same inputs and to produce the same replies and the same effects on tasks as it did before.

artifact.approach: Add rename at the same two layers the other commands already use: a rename(id, title) method on the store object returned by createStore(), and a rename case in run in cli.js. The CLI parses the id with the existing private parseId, joins the remaining arguments into the new title (the same joining convention add uses for its title), and makes one store call; the store finds the task with its existing private find (which already throws the exact 'No task with id <id>' message), normalizes the title through the same code path as add (trim, and the existing empty-title error), assigns only the title on the task in place so id, done state, and list position are preserved, and returns a copy; the CLI replies 'Renamed <id>: <new title>' built from that copy. No other command, output, or file changes.

components.name: Task store
components.responsibility: Owns the in-memory task list and every mutation on it. Gains rename(id, title): change exactly one task's title in place, preserving its id, done state, and position; reuse the existing find-based unknown-id error and the same trimming and empty-title rule add uses.

components.name: Command dispatch
components.responsibility: Turns a command line into one store call plus a formatted reply. Gains the rename case: parse the id with the existing parseId, join the rest of the arguments as the new title, call store.rename(id, title), and reply 'Renamed <id>: <new title>'; all existing cases stay byte-for-byte unchanged.

interfaces.contract: Existing file, modified. Still exports exactly one thing, createStore(). The store it returns keeps add(title), complete(id), remove(id), and all() with today's behavior, and gains one new method: rename(id, title). rename first resolves the id through the same private find that complete and remove use, so an id that matches no task throws Error with the exact message 'No task with id <id>' (for example store.rename(7, 'Call Sam back') throws 'No task with id 7') and nothing changes. It then normalizes the title with the identical rule add uses — coerce to a string treating null and undefined as the empty string, then trim — and if the result is empty it throws Error with the message 'A task needs a title' before any assignment, so the task is left exactly as it was, including title, id, done state, and position. On success it assigns only the title property of the found task in place: the task object is not replaced, so its id and done flag are untouched, it keeps its slot in the internal array, and no other task is affected. It returns a fresh copy { id, title, done } of the updated task, the same shape add and all return. Internally, add and rename share one private helper that does the coerce-trim-and-empty-check so the two rules cannot drift; add keeps its current observable behavior, including the message 'A task needs a title' and not consuming an id when the title is empty.

Existing file, modified. Still exports exactly run(args, store); parseId stays private. The doc comment listing the commands gains one line for rename in the same style as the others. New case in the switch for command === 'rename': run already computes rest as args.slice(1); rest[0] goes through the existing parseId, so a first argument that is not a positive integer throws Error 'Not a task id: <argument>' (['rename', 'abc', 'Call', 'Sam'] throws 'Not a task id: abc') and a missing one (['rename']) throws 'Not a task id: undefined', exactly as done and remove already behave. The new title is rest.slice(1).join(' ') — the whole text after the id, spaces and commas included, and the empty string when nothing follows — and is passed as the second argument to store.rename(id, title). Store errors ('No task with id <id>', 'A task needs a title') propagate unchanged out of run, so ['rename', '2'] and ['rename', '2', '   '] both throw the empty-title error and change nothing. On success run returns the string 'Renamed <id>: <new title>' built from the copy the store returns: ['rename', '2', 'Call', 'Sam', 'back'] returns 'Renamed 2: Call Sam back'; ['rename', '3', 'Buy milk, eggs, and bread'] returns 'Renamed 3: Buy milk, eggs, and bread'; ['rename', '2', '  Call Sam back  '] returns 'Renamed 2: Call Sam back' — the reply always shows the trimmed stored title. The add, done, remove, and list cases and the default branch ('Unknown command: ...') keep their exact current code and output.

decisions.title: Where the rename operation lives
decisions.decision: rename(id, title) is a new method on the store object returned by createStore(); the cli.js case only parses arguments, makes one store call, and formats the reply.
decisions.rationale: Matches the existing layering: every case in cli.js is a single store call plus a template literal, and the store owns all mutation and task-shape knowledge. It also makes rename testable at the store level like add/complete/remove, which is where the id, done, and position preservation guarantees of AC-2 are easiest to pin down.

decisions.title: Unknown-id error and validation order
decisions.decision: rename resolves the id through the store's existing private find before it looks at the title, and the CLI parses the id with the existing parseId before anything else.
decisions.rationale: find already throws exactly 'No task with id <id>' (AC-6) and parseId already throws exactly 'Not a task id: <argument>' (AC-7), so the required messages are reused rather than re-created. Checking the id first mirrors done and remove and keeps the order predictable; the PRD does not cover the case where the id is unknown and the title is also empty, and this choice makes the id error win.

decisions.title: Title trimming and the empty-title error
decisions.decision: Extract add's coerce-trim-and-empty-check into one private helper used by both add and rename; an empty result throws the existing 'A task needs a title', and the check runs before any mutation.
decisions.rationale: The constraints demand trimming identical to add's and an error in the CLI's existing style; sharing the code makes that identity structural instead of coincidental, and reusing add's message avoids inventing a near-duplicate (the PRD deliberately leaves this message open). Validating before mutating is what makes a failed rename leave the task exactly as it was (AC-5). The refactor leaves add's observable behavior unchanged, including not consuming an id on a failed add.

decisions.title: How the new title is read off the command line
decisions.decision: The title is rest.slice(1).join(' ') — everything after the id — and the success reply 'Renamed <id>: <new title>' is built from the copy store.rename returns.
decisions.rationale: This is the same convention add already uses for its title, so multi-word titles with spaces and commas work (AC-3) and trimming behaves identically to add for the same padding (AC-4). Building the reply from the store's return value means the printed title is the stored, trimmed title, so the reply always matches what a later list shows (AC-1).

decisions.title: Scope of the change
decisions.decision: Only src/store.js and src/cli.js change; no new files and no new dependencies; format.js, README.md, package.json, and every existing command's code path stay untouched.
decisions.rationale: Smallest design that meets the acceptance criteria: rename needs no new formatting and no persistence, and AC-9 requires everything that works today to keep working byte-for-byte, which is safest when the existing cases are not edited at all.

risks: The success reply 'Renamed <id>: <new title>' is pinned exactly by AC-1; any wording drift fails acceptance, so tests should assert the full string.

With no id at all, run(['rename']) throws 'Not a task id: undefined', the same literal done and remove produce; AC-8 only requires an error and matching the existing convention is what AC-9 demands, but the literal reads oddly to a person.
When the id is unknown and the title is also empty, the id error wins; the PRD does not specify this case, so tests must not assume the opposite order.
Sharing the title helper between add and rename couples the two rules; that is the point (the constraint demands identical trimming), but a future change to one will change the other.

The title comes from joining argument words, so how the caller splits the command line determines interior spacing; the store's trim normalizes only the ends, exactly as with add — identical behavior, but worth pinning with a test that passes the padded title as a single argument.

reason: the work has no user interface

tasks.title: Add rename(id, title) to the task store with a shared title-normalization helper
tasks.description: Modify src/store.js only; no other file changes. createStore() remains the sole export, and add(title), complete(id), remove(id), and all() keep their exact current observable behavior. First refactor: extract the title normalization add uses into one private helper shared by add and rename — coerce the value to a string treating null and undefined as the empty string, then trim; if the trimmed result is empty, throw Error('A task needs a title') before any mutation. add must keep its current behavior, including that exact message and not consuming an id when the title is empty. Then add one new method rename(id, title) to the returned store: (1) resolve the id through the existing private find that complete and remove use, so an id matching no task throws Error with the exact message 'No task with id <id>' (e.g. store.rename(7, 'Call Sam back') throws 'No task with id 7') and nothing changes; (2) normalize the title with the shared helper — an empty title throws before any assignment, leaving the task exactly as it was, including its title, id, done state, and position; (3) on success assign only the title property on the found task object in place — do not replace the task object or move it in the internal array, so its id and done flag are untouched, it keeps its slot in the list, and no other task is affected; (4) return a fresh copy { id, title, done } of the updated task, the same shape add and all return. The trimming performed by rename must be identical to add's because both go through the one helper.

defects.description: Failing test 'rename of an id no task has replies "No task with id <id>" and changes nothing' (test/rename-cli.test.js, TAP test 10, assertion at line 87). Expected behavior (AC-6): run(['rename','7','Call','Sam','back'], store) throws an Error whose message is exactly 'No task with id 7' and no task changes. Actual behavior: the implementation does exactly that — the reported error is 'Error: No task with id 7', i.e. an Error whose message is 'No task with id 7' — but the test still fails because assert.throws with a RegExp matches the regex against the error's full string representation ('Error: ' + message), so the anchored regex /^No task with id 7$/ can never match any conforming implementation. The test is wrong, not the code; no change to src/cli.js or src/store.js is needed. Fix: assert the message instead of the whole string representation, e.g. assert.throws(fn, { message: 'No task with id 7' }), or a validator function that checks err.message === 'No task with id 7', or change the regex to /^Error: No task with id 7$/.

Failing test 'rename whose first argument is not a task id replies "Not a task id: <argument>" and changes nothing' (test/rename-cli.test.js, TAP test 11, assertion at line 100). Expected behavior (AC-7): run(['rename','abc','Call','Sam'], store) throws an Error whose message is exactly 'Not a task id: abc' and no task changes. Actual behavior: the implementation does exactly that — the reported error is 'Error: Not a task id: abc', an Error with message 'Not a task id: abc' — but the test fails because assert.throws tests a RegExp against the error's string representation 'Error: Not a task id: abc', which the anchored regex /^Not a task id: abc$/ can never match. The test is wrong, not the code. Fix: assert the message, e.g. assert.throws(fn, { message: 'Not a task id: abc' }), or a validator checking err.message === 'Not a task id: abc', or use the regex /^Error: Not a task id: abc$/.

Failing test 'add, done, remove and list keep their exact replies and effects' (test/rename-cli.test.js, TAP test 13, the AC-9 regression test, first failure at line 125). Expected behavior: the pre-existing commands behave exactly as before; the run shows they do — the same behaviors pass in the pre-existing suite (e.g. 'complete and remove refuse an id that does not exist' and 'a bad id or an unknown command is an error' pass) and every non-anchored assertion in this test passes. Actual behavior: the test fails at assert.throws(() => run(['done','abc'], store), /^Not a task id: abc$/) because assert.throws matches a RegExp against the error's string representation 'Error: Not a task id: abc', which this anchored regex can never match; the message itself is correct and unchanged. The same flaw is present later in the same test: assert.throws(() => run(['done','7'], store), /^No task with id 7$/), assert.throws(() => run(['remove','7'], store), /^No task with id 7$/), and assert.throws(() => run(['explode'], store), /^Unknown command: explode$/) will all fail identically once the first is fixed. The test is wrong, not the code; the done/remove/add/list code paths are byte-for-byte unchanged. Fix: make every regex assertion match the full string representation — /^Error: Not a task id: abc$/, /^Error: No task with id 7$/, /^Error: Unknown command: explode$/ — or assert on the message property for each, e.g. assert.throws(fn, { message: 'Not a task id: abc' }).

Failing test 'rename refuses an id that does not exist, exactly like complete and remove' (test/rename-store.test.js, TAP test 18, first failing assertion at line 62). Expected behavior (store contract and AC-6): store.rename(7, 'Call Sam back') throws an Error whose message is exactly 'No task with id 7' and the store is unchanged. Actual behavior: the implementation does exactly that — the reported error is 'Error: No task with id 7', an Error with message 'No task with id 7' — but the test fails because assert.throws matches the RegExp against the error's string representation 'Error: No task with id 7', which the anchored regex /^No task with id 7$/ can never match. The identical second assertion in the same test, assert.throws(() => store.rename(7, '   '), /^No task with id 7$/), has the same flaw and will fail the same way. The test is wrong, not the code; store.rename's unknown-id behavior matches complete and remove exactly. Fix: assert the message, e.g. assert.throws(fn, { message: 'No task with id 7' }) for both assertions, or validators checking err.message === 'No task with id 7', or change both regexes to /^Error: No task with id 7$/.

artifact.title: Add a rename command to the task CLI
artifact.summary: Adds 'rename <id> <new title>' to the task CLI: it changes one task's title in place and replies 'Renamed <id>: <new title>'. The task's id, done state, and position in the list are preserved, and no other task or command is affected. The implementation deliberately reuses existing conventions rather than adding new ones: id parsing goes through the CLI's existing parseId, title trimming goes through the store's normalization helper now shared with add, and error messages match the existing commands exactly ('No task with id <id>' for an unknown id, 'Not a task id: <argument>' for a non-id first argument, and add's 'A task needs a title' for a missing or blank new title). Test coverage maps each acceptance criterion AC-1 through AC-9 to specific tests. Reviewers should start with the normalizeTitle extraction in src/store.js (the only rewrite of existing behavior) and then the new rename case in src/cli.js.
changes: src/store.js: extracted the title normalization add uses into one private normalizeTitle(title) helper (coerce with String(title ?? ''), trim, throw Error('A task needs a title') when the result is empty) and routed add through it, keeping add's observable behavior identical, including not consuming an id when the title is empty. Added one new method rename(id, title): it resolves the id through the existing private find so an unknown id throws the exact 'No task with id <id>' and nothing changes; it normalizes the title with the shared helper before any assignment, so an empty title throws and leaves the task exactly as it was; on success it assigns only the title on the found task object in place, never replacing or moving it, so id, done flag, and slot in the internal array are preserved and no other task is touched; and it returns a fresh { id, title, done } copy, the same shape add and all return. complete, remove, and all are untouched; createStore() remains the sole export.

src/cli.js: added a rename case to the command dispatch. It passes the first argument through the existing private parseId, so a non-id argument throws 'Not a task id: <argument>' and a missing one throws 'Not a task id: undefined', exactly like done and remove. It builds the new title as rest.slice(1).join(' ') without pre-trimming, so trimming happens in the store through the same helper add uses. It makes a single store.rename(id, title) call and builds the reply 'Renamed <id>: <new title>' from the returned copy, so the reply always shows the stored, trimmed title. Store errors ('No task with id <id>', 'A task needs a title') propagate unchanged. One line for rename was added to the doc comment in the existing style; the add, done, remove, and list cases and the default branch are untouched.

Tests: coverage is mapped to every acceptance criterion. Covered behaviors include the reply format and the new title appearing in the list afterwards (AC-1); preservation of id, done state, and position, and that only the title changes (AC-2); titles containing spaces and commas (AC-3); trimming identical to add (AC-4); missing or blank titles leaving the task exactly as it was (AC-5); unknown ids (AC-6); non-id first arguments (AC-7); no arguments at all (AC-8); and unchanged replies and effects for add, done, remove, and list, including add's trimming, its empty-title error, its no-id-consumed behavior, and the other commands working in a session that also uses rename (AC-9).
risks: The only rewrite of existing behavior is in src/store.js: add's title handling was extracted into the shared normalizeTitle helper and add now routes through it. A regression here could change add's trimming, its 'A task needs a title' error, or make add consume an id when the title is empty. Tests cover these behaviors, but this is the highest-value place to review first.

The rename case is added inside the command dispatch switch in src/cli.js, which all commands share; a mistake in that switch could affect existing commands. Per the change summary the other cases and the default branch are untouched, and regression tests cover add, done, remove, and list both in isolation and alongside rename.

'rename' with no arguments at all replies 'Not a task id: undefined' (parseId applied to a missing first argument), which matches the existing done/remove convention; the PRD only required that an error be reported. Confirm this exact wording is acceptable.

A missing or blank new title reports 'A task needs a title', add's message, reused because the PRD left the exact wording open and required the CLI's existing error style. Confirm it reads acceptably for rename; changing it is a one-line message swap in store.js.
The test coverage artifact maps tests to every acceptance criterion but does not include execution results; reviewers should confirm the suite is green in CI before merging.
